headline: An Ebola outbreak with no vaccine to stop it

sources.title: Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus, Democratic Republic of the Congo
Ebola disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda
Over a thousand people dead: Congo's Ebola crisis worsens | DW News (video, DW News)

chunks.text: An Ebola [[outbreak]] in central Africa has killed more than 1,500 people since May, and this time doctors have no vaccine to {{fall back on}}. The disease {{broke out}} in Ituri, a province in the northeast of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and the World Health Organization declared a global health [[emergency]] on May 17, 2026. By 30 July the number of [[confirmed cases]] had {{gone up}} to 3,626, and 1,589 people had died. The [[death rate]] is 44 percent, so [[close to]] half of the patients do not [[survive]].

verbs.correct: To use when nothing else works
To rise to a higher number
verbs.wrong: To continue for a long time

chunks.text: Most Ebola outbreaks come from the Zaire [[species]] of the virus, and a vaccine for that one has been [[approved]] since 2019. This outbreak is different. It comes from a species called Bundibugyo, and the vaccine that health teams {{rolled out}} in past outbreaks does nothing against it. There is no proven [[treatment]] [[either]]. Scientists are {{carrying out}} tests on possible new vaccines, but none of them is ready. Until one arrives, teams have to {{make do with}} older methods: find patients early, keep them apart from others, and {{track down}} every person they met.

chunks.text: The virus has now [[spread]] to five provinces, and Ituri is a busy trading region where people cross [[borders]] every day. Twenty cases {{turned up}} in [[neighboring]] Uganda, where two people died, and a single case was recorded in France. [[Health workers]] have [[paid a heavy price]]: 151 of them have caught the virus and 44 have died. Teams have [[identified]] 17,863 [[contacts]] and are {{checking up on}} more than 13,000 of them.

verbs.wrong: To arrive and report your name

chunks.text: Uganda has not reported a new case since June 21, which [[suggests]] the [[chain of infection]] there has been broken. In the Congo the work continues. European health experts say the risk to people in Europe is very low, because Ebola only {{passes on}} through [[close contact]] with blood and other [[body fluids]], not through the air. Aid teams have {{set up}} [[isolation units]] and are training [[local staff]], and health agencies say the outbreak will only {{die out}} when [[every last]] chain is found.

mainIdea.s: An Ebola outbreak in the Congo has killed more than 1,500 people since May 2026. It comes from a rare virus species with no vaccine, so teams track down every contact by hand.
mainIdea.why: The story says this outbreak is the Bundibugyo species, which has no vaccine, so teams rely on tracing contacts instead.

mainIdea.s: More than 1,500 people have died in this Ebola outbreak in Central Africa, and there is no vaccine. Health experts say the disease spreads through the air between people nearby.
mainIdea.why: Close, but Ebola does not spread through the air. The article says it only passes on through close contact with blood and body fluids.

mainIdea.s: Health teams in West Africa ended a separate Ebola outbreak last year using an approved vaccine. That outbreak affected far fewer people and never spread beyond a single country.
mainIdea.why: This story is about the current outbreak in the Congo, which has no vaccine and has already spread to two countries.
